description:
Certificate of
Lawful Existing Development: Continued use of the land as seperate to the main dwellings
decision_conditions: <p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The applicant has failed to demonstrate, on the balance of probabilities, that the land has been used continuously as a separate planning unit independent of the main dwelling(s) for the requisite period. The evidence submitted is insufficient to establish the nature, extent and continuity of the claimed use or to demonstrate that the land functions independently from the residential curtilage of the dwelling(s). Accordingly, the Local Planning Authority is not satisfied that the requirements of Section 191 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended) have been met.&nbsp;</span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The proposal is NOT therefore development nor lawful</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The application seeks a Certificate of Lawful Existing Use or Development for the continued use of land as separate from the main dwelling(s). The information submitted has not demonstrated any operational development or material change of use of the land. The separation of land from an existing planning unit, in itself, does not constitute development as defined by Section 55 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990. Consequently, the subject matter of the application does not comprise development capable of benefiting from a Certificate of Lawful Existing Use or Development under Section 191 of the Act.&nbsp;</span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">The proposal is NOT therefore development nor lawful.&nbsp;</span></p>
